newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES STOP AVALANCHE UNDEFEATED STREAK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES STOP AVALANCHE UNDEFEATED STREAK.

text.p: Jason Dawe and Brian Holzinger scored in the third period as the Buffalo Sabres beat the Colorado Avalanche 5-4 Thursday, snapping the defending champions' franchise-record 11-game unbeaten streak.

With the game tied 3-3, Dawe worked the puck free from the boards behind the Colorado goal, came out in front and put a backhander on net. Craig Billington made the initial save, but Dawe jammed in the rebound for his second goal of the game 5:18 into the third period for a 4-3 lead .

Holzinger's goal at 9:25 gave Buffalo a 5-3 lead. Dixon Ward fed a pass to a cutting Holzinger at centre ice. Holzinger skated into the Colorado zone and was tripped, but the puck carried past Billington and into the net while Holzinger went sliding into the boards.
"It's nice to see those finally getting through," Holzinger said. "We had a few lucky breaks go our way, a few weak goals go in on him."

Sandis Ozolinsh had a goal and two assists for Colorado, which was 9-0-2 in its previous 11 games to match the franchise-record unbeaten streak set by the Quebec Nordiques, who went 7-0-4 from March 10-31, 1981.
Rene Corbet scored at 10:51 of the final period to pull Colorado within one.
The Avalanche, playing their third game in four nights, also had a five-game winning streak halted.
Mike Peca and Mike Wilson also tallied for the Sabres, who defeated the two best teams in the league this week -- Colorado and the Florida Panthers on Monday.

Buffalo was without captain Pat LaFontaine and defenceman Garry Galley. LaFontaine missed his fourth straight game with exhaustion and Galley missed his fourth in a row with a strained right shoulder.

At New Jersey, Mike Fountain recorded a shutout in his NHL debut and Alexander Mogilny scored twice as the Vancouver Canucks notched a 3-0 victory over the Devils, who had their five-game winning streak snapped.
The 24-year-old Fountain was recalled Wednesday from Syracuse of the American Hockey League to replace the injured Kirk McLean.
He made 40 saves, 31 over the final two periods, as the Canucks shut out New Jersey for just the second time in team history. McLean had the other one in 1988.
Former Devil Alexander Semak scored into an empty net with 26 seconds left to seal the victory.
In Boston, Adam Oates's goal 65 seconds into overtime lifted the Bruins to a 2-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins, who remained winless on the road this season.
Pittsburgh fell to 0-10-1 on the road this season, the worst road start in franchise history. The win was just Boston's second in 10 home games (2-5-3).
The Penguins tied the game on Kevin Hatcher's goal in the final minute of regulation. Troy Mallette scored Boston's first goal.
In Chicago, German Titov scored with four seconds left in overtime as the Calgary Flames pulled out a 2-1 victory over the Blackhawks.
Calgary is 5-0-3 in its last eight games at Chicago and has not lost there since April 3, 1994. The win was the Flames' first this month (1-3-1).
Kevin Miller put Chicago up 1-0 just 4:32 into the game. Dave Gagner tied the game 5:02 into the third period.
In Phoenix, Jeff O'Neill scored a shorthanded goal and Sean Burke stopped 40 shots as the Hartford Whalers continued their impressive start with a 2-1 defeat of the Coyotes.
The win was the second straight for the Whalers, lead the Northeast Division with 20 points.

Keith Primeau and O'Neil put Hartford up 2-0 before Teppo Numminen's first goal of the season, with 6:26 left in regulation, ruined Burke's attempt at a second shutout against Phoenix in as many games.

In St Louis, Stephane Matteau, Pierre Turgeon and Jim Campbell scored a team-record 39 seconds apart in the third period as the Blues staged a furious comeback for a 5-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
With the Lightning holding a 3-1 lead, Al MacInnis scored a power-play goal at 9:11 to make it a one-goal game.

Matteau tallied his eighth goal of the season to tie the game 3-3 with 6:45 remaining. Twelve seconds later, Turgeon redirected Brett Hull's shot for a 4-3 lead. Campbell completed the scoring 27 seconds later with his eighth goal.
In Philadelphia, Steve Konowalchuk had a goal and an assist and Joe Juneau set up a pair of scores as the Washington Capitals defeated the Flyers 5-2 for the second time this season.
Phil Housley, Chris Simon, Sergei Gonchar and Craig Berube also scored for Washington.

At Los Angeles, Kevin Stevens scored the go-ahead goal midway through the first period and Byron Dafoe added 28 saves as the Kings won back-to-back games at home for the first in a month, defeating the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-1.
